1.01.t: Long Bone in Hand — Parts, Physis, Apophysis
1.01.b:
### Hold a long bone → name 4 parts
1) **Diaphysis** → the shaft → thick cortex around the medullary cavity
[[FIG: Fig 1.1, 1.2 · 1.01
2) **Metaphysis** → the flare → thin cortex, cancellous bone, the fastest blood flow
3) **Physis** → the cartilage growth plate → closes to a **physeal scar** on X-ray
4) **Epiphysis** → the end beyond the physis → joint surface, from a **secondary centre**

- Metacarpals, metatarsals and phalanges → **one physis** each → thumb metacarpal at the **base** · other metacarpals at the **head**

### Physis vs apophysis (Nagah p3)
| | Physis | Apophysis  |
[[FIG: Fig 1.3, 1.4 · 1.01
|---|---|---|
| Growth | **Length** of the bone | **No** length → only its own shape |
| Force on it | Compression ("pressure epiphysis") | **Traction** ("traction epiphysis") |
| Typical injury | Salter-Harris fracture | **Avulsion** in teenage sport · traction apophysitis |

- Patella → a **sesamoid** bone, not an apophysis
- Traction apophysitis → **Osgood-Schlatter** (tibial tuberosity) · **Sever** (calcaneus) · **Sinding-Larsen-Johansson** (lower patellar pole)

PITFALL — "the physis is intra-articular"
- Nagah p3 → physis intra-articular · most physes lie **outside** the joint
- Say → "**physis = length, apophysis = traction; physis inside the joint only where the metaphysis is intracapsular**"

### Periosteum — 2 layers (Nagah p3)
[[FIG: Fig 1.5 · 1.01
| Layer | Made of | Job |
|---|---|---|
| **Outer fibrous** | Collagen → Sharpey fibres anchor tendons | Carries the **periosteal vessels** |
| **Inner cambium** | Osteoprogenitor cells | **Osteogenic** → appositional growth (**width**) and callus |

- Child → thick, loosely attached → **greenstick fracture** · **subperiosteal abscess** · adult → thin, firmly attached → **sinus**

1.02.t: Blood Supply of a Long Bone
1.02.b:
### Four systems (Nagah p4)
| System | Feeds | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Nutrient** (endosteal) | **Inner 2/3** of the cortex + marrow | Main adult supply · high pressure |
| **Periosteal** | **Outer 1/3** of the cortex | Low pressure · vital in children |
| **Metaphyseal** | Metaphysis | Joins the nutrient system |
| **Epiphyseal** | Epiphysis + **germinal layer** of the physis | End arteries while the physis is open |

- Nagah lists only nutrient + periosteal → **add metaphyseal and epiphyseal**
  [[FIG: Fig 1.6 · 1.02
- Nutrient foramen points **away from the growing end** → "to the elbow I go, from the knee I flee"
- Normal flow → **centrifugal** · intramedullary reaming → **centripetal** → endosteal supply back in ≈3 weeks (Nagah p14)

CLINICAL PEARL — reamed femur, unreamed tibia (Nagah p14)
- Femur → thick muscle cover keeps the periosteal supply → **ream**
- Tibia → thin cover, periosteum often stripped → **unreamed** nail keeps the endosteal supply

### Blood & the physis
- **No vessel crosses an open physis** → epiphyseal artery dies → **germinal layer dies → growth stops**
  [[FIG: Fig 1.7, 1.8 · 1.02
- Articular and epiphyseal cartilage → fed by **synovial fluid** → survive ischaemia
- Metaphyseal **hairpin loops** → sluggish flow → children's osteomyelitis starts in the **metaphysis**

CLINICAL PEARL — why the distal tibia heals badly (Nagah p16)
- **End arteries** with little collateral flow
- **Thin soft-tissue cover** → no muscle to bring periosteal vessels
- Poor venous return in the lowest part of the limb

1.03.b:
### Two ways to make bone (Nagah p4)
| | Intramembranous | Endochondral |
|---|---|---|
| Model | No cartilage | **Cartilage model** first |
| Bones | Skull vault, **clavicle** | Long bones, vertebrae, pelvis |
| In fracture healing | **Hard callus** (rigid fixation) | **Soft callus** (cast, nail) |
| Width or length | **Appositional** = width | Physis = **length** |

- Ossification starts ≈ **6th embryonic week**; clavicle first · calcification = calcium in abnormal tissue (Nagah p4)
  [[FIG: Fig 1.9, 1.10 · 1.03
- Growth → humerus **80% proximal** · femur **70% distal** · tibia **55% proximal** → "**toward the knee, away from the elbow**"
  [[FIG: Fig 1.11 · 1.03

### Zones of the growth plate → epiphysis to metaphysis
[[FIG: Fig 1.12, 1.13 · 1.03
| Zone | Job | Disease in this zone |
|---|---|---|
| **Reserve / germinal** | Stem cells | Epiphyseal **ischaemia** → arrest |
| **Proliferative** | Cell **columns** → **length** | **Achondroplasia** |
| **Hypertrophic** → **provisional calcification** | Cells swell 5–10× · little matrix | **Fractures** · SCFE (slipped capital femoral epiphysis) · rickets |
| **Metaphysis** | Vessels invade → bone | Osteomyelitis |

- Normal physis ≈ **2 mm** · rickets ≈ **5 mm** · child → the **physis fails before the ligament**

PITFALL — which zone fails?
- Classic + Nagah p18 → **hypertrophic zone** · Campbell 15th → "the proliferative zone"
- Say → "**hypertrophic zone, at provisional calcification** → germinal layer stays with the epiphysis → growth goes on"

- **Salter-Harris II** → metaphyseal spike = **Thurston-Holland** fragment · **Harris (Park) lines** tilted = **partial arrest**
  [[FIG: Fig 1.14 · 1.03

1.04.t: Intracapsular Metaphysis — Why Osteomyelitis Becomes Septic Arthritis
1.04.b:
### The 4 joints (Nagah p7)
| Joint | Intracapsular metaphysis |
|---|---|
| **Hip** | Proximal femoral neck |
| **Shoulder** | Proximal humeral metaphysis |
| **Elbow** | Radial neck |
| **Ankle** | Distal fibula (lateral malleolus) |

- Mnemonic → "**HSEA**" · the **knee has none**
  [[FIG: Fig 1.15 · 1.04

### Four routes to septic arthritis (Nagah p7)
1) **Infant** → vessels still cross the physis → metaphysis → epiphysis → joint
[[FIG: Fig 1.16 · 1.04
2) **Intracapsular metaphysis** → abscess opens inside the capsule
3) A structure runs from the metaphysis into the joint → **long head of biceps**
4) **Septicaemia** → seeds the synovium directly

PITFALL — up to what age do vessels cross the physis?
- Campbell ch 24 → under **18 months**; Campbell ch 23 → under **2 years**
- Say → "**transphyseal vessels until about 18 months to 2 years**"

1.07.b:
### Two classifications side by side
| Sunderland | Seddon | What is cut | Tinel | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Neurapraxia** | Myelin only → conduction block | None | **Full**, weeks to 3 months |
| **2** | **Axonotmesis** | Axon · endoneurium intact | **Advances** | Full · proximal → distal |
| **3** | Axonotmesis | Axon + endoneurium | Advances | Incomplete · mismatched fibres |
| **4** | Axonotmesis | + perineurium · only epineurium left | **Stays** (neuroma) | Poor → **surgery** |
| **5** | **Neurotmesis** | Whole trunk | Stays | None → **surgery** |

- **6th degree** (Mackinnon) → mixed levels in one nerve · neurapraxia → **motor > sensory**, sympathetic spared
  [[FIG: Fig 1.28 · 1.07

### Wallerian degeneration
1) Distal segment breaks up from **day 2–3** · electrical response lost after **3 days**
[[FIG: Fig 1.29, 1.30 · 1.07
2) Schwann cells clear debris → **bands of Büngner** wait for the axon
3) Proximal stump dies back to the **first node of Ranvier**
4) Sprouts grow **≈1 mm/day ≈ 1 inch a month**

- EMG (electromyography) **fibrillations** at **2–4 weeks** · motor end-plates survive ≈ **12–18 months** → then **tendon transfer**

PITFALL — regeneration speed
- Campbell → "1 inch a month"; Nerves 2025 → "1 mm a day, 3 cm a month"
- Say → "**1 mm a day, about an inch a month**"

### Tinel & the order of recovery
[[FIG: Fig 1.31 · 1.07
- **Advancing** Tinel = Sunderland 2–3 · **stuck** Tinel = neuroma → explore
- Muscles recover in the **order their branches leave** → radial nerve → **brachioradialis first, extensor indicis last** (Nagah p38)

### Tourniquet palsy vs post-tourniquet syndrome (Nagah p7)
[[FIG: Fig 1.32 · 1.07
| | **Tourniquet palsy** | **Post-tourniquet syndrome** |
|---|---|---|
| Cause | **Pressure** under the cuff | **Ischaemia** of the whole limb |
| Motor | **Paralysis** | Weakness |
| Sensory | **Dissociation** → touch and position lost, pain kept | Numbness, paraesthesia |
| Other | — | **Oedema, pallor, joint stiffness** |
| Recovery | Up to **3 months** (Nagah p7) | Within **1 week** |

### Double crush (Nagah p37)
- **Double crush** → proximal squeeze (e.g. C6–7 root) slows **axonal transport** → distal nerve more vulnerable → carpal tunnel
  [[FIG: Fig 1.33 · 1.07
- Failed carpal tunnel release → look for the **second level** (neck, thoracic outlet, pronator) (Nagah p37)

1.13.b:
| Test | Why it works (anatomy) | What it shows | Trap |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Tinel** | Regrowing axon tips have no myelin → mechanosensitive | Level of regeneration / compression | Stuck Tinel → neuroma (Sunderland 4–5) |
| **Wrinkle test** | Skin wrinkling in water needs **sympathetic** fibres to the skin | Complete lesion → no wrinkling (useful in children) | Recovers late |
| **Sweat (ninhydrin) test** | Sweat glands = sympathetic, run in the same nerve | Sweating in the autonomous zone → incomplete lesion (Campbell) | — |
| **Triple response of Lewis** | Axon reflex runs DRG → skin | Kept → **pre-ganglionic** lesion (Handbook) | — |
| **Vibration 256 Hz** | Large myelinated fibres, hurt first by compression | **First sense lost** in compression neuropathy (Nagah p37) | — |

- **Two-point discrimination** → density of slowly adapting receptors in the pulp → shows innervation density → normal static 2PD < 6 mm (Campbell) · needs a cooperative patient
- Test every nerve in its **autonomous zone**
